mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, or SPX posts negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where GDP y/y growth accelerates by > 2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate over the previous 3 months, indicating a rapidly tightening labor market, will lead to wage inflation and reduced corporate profitability, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 55% of instances where UNRATE drops > 0.5pp in 3 months, or core PCE inflation remains below 2% y/y despite falling UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A widening gap between industrial production and real GDP, indicating supply constraints, will lead to rising input costs and reduced corporate profitability, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where INDPRO > GDPC1 by > 2pp, or input cost pressures do not materialize (ISM Prices Paid < 50).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the federal funds rate, indicating a hawkish Fed policy shift, will lead to a flattening yield curve and reduced equity risk premiums, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, or the yield curve steepens (10y-2y) despite rising FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts, indicating a strong residential investment cycle, will boost economic activity and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where HOUST rises > 10% y/y, or residential investment does not contribute positively to GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment, indicating a rapidly strengthening labor market, will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 20-day returns in > 45% of instances where PAYEMS rises by > 200k jobs m/m, or consumer spending does not accelerate (real retail sales growth < 3% y/y).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in consumer price inflation, indicating a loss of purchasing power, will lead to reduced consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 60-day returns in > 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% m/m, or real consumer spending does not decline (real retail sales growth > 2% y/y).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in real consumer spending, indicating a rapidly weakening economy, will lead to reduced corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines > 5% y/y, or corporate earnings do not decline (S&P 500 EPS growth > 5% y/y).
